newsitem.title: ESTONIA: STOCKS BOOSTED BY JUNE RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS BOOSTED BY JUNE RESULTS.

text.p: * Total trade on the Estonian bourse on Thursday was 60.2
million kroons versus Wednesday's 36.3 million kroons.
* The Talse index gained 1.01 percent to close at 276.03.
* Forekspank was the most active stock with 15.4
million kroons traded to close 0.35 kroons higher at 149.40
kroons.
* Hoiupank turned over 7.1 million kroons to
finish 2.5 kroons higher at 154.00 kroons after releasing a
record monthly profit result of 18.8 million kroons for June.
* Tallinna Pank also hit the news with an
announcement that is was to take over Latvia's Saules Bank.
Tallinna's trade was 965,336 kroons to end 0.65 kroons higher
at 63.10 kroons.
* Hansapank and Tallinna Pank also released their
June results.
* 19 stocks traded, 3 steady, 11 up, 6 down.
Most banking shares were higher
on the Estonian stock exchange on Thursday as the market
responded to the first batch of June results, dealers said.
Total trade on the main list was 47.9 million kroons with
the Talse index 1.01 percent higher at 279.03.
Dealers said the results released by Hoiupank and Hansapank
were broadly in line with market expectations while Tallinna
Pank's, which showed a June profit of 4.4 million kroons, were
a little disappointing.
But Tallinna's price was pushed up 0.65 kroons to 63.10
kroons on news that it planned to acquire a 100 percent stake
in Saules Bank, one of the largest banks in Latvia.
Hoiupank's June result, a record 18.8 milion kroons, was
released 30 miutes before the bourse closed. It finished 2.5
kroons higher at 154.00 kroons in trade of 7.1 million kroons.
"If they continue like this, they will have to revise heir
profit forecast upwards," one analyst said.
Hansapank released its results after the bourse closed. It
showed a June profit of 23.1 kroons compared to 41.8 million
kroons in May.
Hansa saw trade of 12.1 million kroons to rise 2.05 kroons
to 149.40 kroons.
Forekspank was the most active stock in trade of 15.4
million kroons to close at 194.75 kroons, up 0.35 kroons.
"There was a lot of speculative selling and buying interest
ahead of the release of its results," one trader said.
The free market was dominated by trade in privatisation
securities with 12.3 million kroons turned over.
Compensation securities rose to 0.322 kroons from 0.316
kroons with a volume of 8.3 million kroons.
"Holders of securities are wondering what to do--they can
sell now or buy into Eesti Gaas, so interest will be strong in
these for a little while longer," a trader said.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202/1
reuters@reuters.ee
